current.text: He ran a lot of point guard in the preseason and has the ball in his hands a lot.
Playing well in the preseason. The bigger ball handling role should bring extra assists.
He goes around picks 53 to 60 in mock drafts.
Experts disagree on whether that price is a bargain. One speaker sees good value in the 60s and others call 55 to 60 a steal. Josh thinks 53 to 60 is about right.
Picks 47 to 49 are a bit early for him.
His upside is about top 40, not top 30 or top 35. His floor is about rank 60. Taking him in rounds 4 to 6 makes sense.
Josh says he only reaches the top 30 if Paolo Banchero gets hurt. His main downside is his own injury risk.
In an auction, 11 to 15 USD is a fair price. In one mock he went for 15 USD, which Josh called about right.
He is a projected starter next to Jalen Suggs, Desmond Bane, Paolo Banchero and Wendell Carter Jr. This group was very good when it played together.
New head coach Sean Sweeney replaces Jamahl Mosley. His effect on pace, offense and roles is unknown.
Orlando plays 3, 4 and 4 games in our playoff weeks (11 games) and has 14 back-to-backs. The experts call the schedule unremarkable.

durable.text: He has no single standout category but is good across the board. He does not add much in steals and blocks and is not a high-volume 3-point shooter.
Points, FT% and assists for a forward are his best categories. Blocks and turnovers are his weakest, but neither is a real outlier.
Injuries ruined two straight seasons. In 2025-26 a high ankle sprain from contact cost him about 47 to 51 games. He came back too early, hurt the ankle again, then hurt his calf in the playoffs.
Phil sees the last two years of injuries as random. Before that he was reliable and played through ankle rolls.
He is probably better in category leagues than in points leagues.

tags.name: injury last season
tags.detail: High ankle sprain, reinjured after an early return, then a calf injury in the playoffs. Played 34 games.

tags.name: sites disagree on price
tags.detail: Yahoo value 21 USD (rank 50), ESPN value 6 USD (rank 68).

note: The experts see Wagner as a fairly priced top 40 to top 60 player. Their auction range is 11 to 15 USD, close to the Yahoo average cost of 12.8 USD and the ESPN average cost of 8.9 USD, and far below the 26 USD our league paid last season. He has no weak category, so he fits any build, and his points, FT% and assists as a forward are what you pay for. Bid up to about 15 USD. Early in the season, check that he keeps the point guard role under new coach Sweeney and that his ankle holds up.
